title: A Night in the Desert I Won't Forget
script: Narrator: [warmly] I never expected to love the desert, because I always imagined it as empty, boring, and simply too hot to enjoy.
Narrator: A female friend and I joined a registered small-group trip with a local guide after checking weather, transport, communication, and campsite rules.
Narrator: [concerned] We drove for hours through flat, dry land, and I kept wondering why anyone would choose to live somewhere so harsh and quiet.
Narrator: Then, as the sun began setting, the whole landscape changed color completely, turning orange, then deep red, then a soft purple.
Narrator: [honestly] I had never seen colors like that in the sky before, and I forgot to complain about the heat for the first time all day.

Narrator: Our guide assigned the group a permitted campsite near low rocks and reviewed the night safety plan, and my friend suggested we wait outside until it got fully dark instead of sleeping early.
Narrator: [relieved] I was tired and almost said no, but something about the quiet desert air made me want to stay awake a little longer.
Narrator: When darkness finally came, I looked up and genuinely gasped. I had never seen so many stars in my entire life.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Because there were no city lights anywhere nearby, even faint stars I didn't know existed became clearly visible above us.
Narrator: Our guide pointed out a pale band of light stretching across the whole sky, which she said was actually our own galaxy.
Narrator: [reflective] I felt incredibly small in that moment, although not in a frightening way, more like a comforting kind of smallness.
Narrator: We stayed outside for almost three hours, mostly silent, just watching the sky slowly turn above our heads.
Narrator: [peacefully] I understood then why some people choose the desert, despite its harsh daytime heat and endless, empty distances.
Narrator: Sometimes the emptiest-looking places hide the fullest skies, and I almost missed that because I judged the desert too quickly.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator agree to the desert road trip?
options: Her friend refused to travel alone and she felt guilty saying no
quiz.explanation: She agreed because her friend refused to travel alone, and she felt too guilty to say no.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator’s first view of the desert prove incomplete?

The friend described the stars incorrectly

quiz.explanation: Dark skies reveal light hidden in cities.
